## A — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].

The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].

sections.heading: B — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
sections.markdown:
## B — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with interstates, road markings and railroad crossings as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants study interstate entry and exit, emergency stops, lane-control markings and railroad crossings.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

## C — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Use an entrance ramp to enter an interstate and watch for signs that indicate an exit ramp is being entered the wrong way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
DO NOT ENTER and WRONG WAY signs can warn that you are about to travel the wrong direction on a ramp. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
If already traveling the wrong way on a ramp, pull onto the shoulder, stop and turn around only when no traffic is approaching. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
An acceleration lane lets an entering driver match the speed of interstate traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Check over the shoulder for an interstate traffic gap before merging. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
Adjust speed to the selected gap and signal the merge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
Do not stop during interstate entry unless there is no traffic gap. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
Merge at approximately the same speed as the other interstate traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
Be ready for a vehicle ahead on the entrance ramp to slow or stop without warning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A01
Traffic already on the interstate has priority over vehicles entering it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A01
Do not assume interstate drivers will see you or move over to create entry space. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A02
On the interstate, maintain a steady pace while obeying the posted speed limit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A02
Leave at least a two-second gap behind the vehicle ahead on the interstate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A02
In bad weather or on slick pavement, double or triple interstate following time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A02
The handbook identifies rear-end impacts as the most frequent interstate crash type. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A02
Watch vehicles entering the interstate and move left to help them merge only when that move is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A02
Avoid unnecessary interstate lane changes and remain right unless overtaking another vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A02
Signal an interstate lane change and check blind spots before moving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

sections.domain: Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings — C.02
sections.heading: C — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
sections.markdown:
## C — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A02
After passing on the interstate, see the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror before returning ahead of it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A02
If an interstate exit is missed, continue to the next exit rather than backing up. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A02
Do not drive across an interstate median. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A02
If drowsy, stop and take a break. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A02
If very sleepy, leave the highway and obtain sleep, such as at a motel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A03
For an interstate exit, signal and move to the correct lane at least a mile before the exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A03
When leaving the interstate, slow after entering the deceleration lane rather than slowing in the through lanes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A03
After exiting, watch for two-way traffic and reassess speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A03
For an interstate breakdown or other emergency, move as far onto the right shoulder as possible and get all four wheels well off the roadway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A03
The handbook permits slowly moving even with a flat tire to reduce the hazard of stopping on a bridge or underpass. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A03
At an interstate emergency stop, turn on the four-way warning flashers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A03
At night, the interstate emergency-stop guidance calls for flares or reflectors. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A03
Do not open a door or leave the stopped vehicle on the side facing traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A03
For assistance after an interstate emergency stop, raise both trunk lid and hood, or attach a white cloth to the antenna. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A03
If the vehicle cannot be moved off the roadway, remove passengers and move them away from the area in case it is struck. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A03
Sign shapes can convey general meaning when darkness or weather makes the words hard to read. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A03
Diamond-shaped signs warn about hazards, while rectangular signs provide regulatory information such as lawful speed or direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0062]

Misconceptions: An acceleration lane helps match traffic speed but does not give entering traffic priority; raised crossing gates alone do not satisfy the complete departure conditions.
Mnemonics: Recall index: gap, signal, match, merge; this organizer restates the entry procedure.
Glossary: Recall terms: acceleration lane, deceleration lane, crossbuck, stop line, solid marking and broken marking.
Dynamic facts: Roadside signage and present legal applicability remain edition-sensitive. No shortcut is taught as a remedy for sleepiness; the source's stop-and-rest instructions are retained.

sections.domain: Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings — C2.01
sections.heading: C2 — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings help identify the correct vehicle position on the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
An overhead lane arrow with ONLY requires travel in the arrow's indicated direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
An arrow painted on the roadway has the same directional meaning as an overhead arrow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, drive on the right and leave the left half to opposing traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
On a multilane road, select the lane with the smoothest traffic flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
With three or more lanes traveling one direction, the middle lane or lanes usually have the smoothest flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A01
The source describes the left lane as serving faster traffic, passing and left turns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
Slower traffic and drivers turning right use the right lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A01
With two lanes traveling one direction, the right lane usually has the smoothest flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A01
Where special left-turn lanes exist, the left lane may have the smoothest traffic flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A01
White road lines separate traffic traveling in the same direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A01
Yellow road lines separate traffic traveling in opposite directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A01
A broken line allows passing or a lane change when the way is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A01
A solid white line indicates that passing or changing lanes is hazardous. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A01
A solid yellow line bars passing or lane changing except for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A02
The handbook's marking example prohibits passing when a solid yellow line is on the driver's side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A02
The handbook's opposing-side solid-yellow passing example still requires the way ahead to be clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A02
Double yellow lines separating traffic prohibit passing in the handbook's example. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A03
At an advance railroad warning, slow down, look and listen, and prepare to stop if a train approaches. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A03
The railroad approach marking described is R-X-R followed by a stop line nearer the tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A03
Wait behind the marked stop line while a train passes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A03
A railroad crossbuck functions as a yield sign requiring drivers to yield to trains. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A03
At a crossbuck, slow down, look and listen, and stop when a train is approaching. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A03
A sign below a crossbuck indicates the track count where more than one track is present. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A03
Stop for flashing red railroad signals and yield to the approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A03
At a crossing with multiple tracks, verify that every track is clear before crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A03
When crossing lights begin flashing, stop before the place where the gate will lower across the lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A03
Remain stopped until the crossing gates are raised and the warning lights have stopped flashing, then cross only when safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]
